diagnosis: The image shows an extremely degenerate jam: hundreds of pairs lie within about $10^{-16}$ of the maximum, points carry 15–33 contacts against only 12 tangent degrees of freedom each, so the linearized LP has essentially no feasible descent direction and small kicks are inevitably polished back to the same contact graph. It is also inequitably loaded: one rattler has zero contacts while others have more than 30, meaning a 72-point core is doing all the work and lowering the maximum requires a coordinated expansion of that core to make room for all 73 points, not an isolated move. Prior programs all funneled perturbed copies of this same configuration through the same smooth-objective plus LP-polish pipeline, so they repeatedly rediscovered the same basin, and several spent their whole budget on expensive candidates and timed out before returning an improved incumbent. The missing structural property is therefore a different, more balanced and approximately isotropic contact/stress topology in which every point is active and contacts are shared equitably, rather than a marginally perturbed version of the present over-jammed graph.

It is also structurally unbalanced—one point is a rattler with no contacts, so the score is determined by a jammed 72-point core while the remaining point contributes nothing, and contact loads and geometry are highly heterogeneous rather than point-equivalent. What is missing is a stress-balanced, approximately isostatic contact graph—hundreds of pairs tied at the maximum to \(10^{-10}\)–\(10^{-12}\), with positive contact stresses whose tangent resultants vanish at every point and no free rattler directions. Progress now needs either exact equiripple convergence, a genuinely different configuration topology, or a controlled move that changes which pairs form that graph.

diagnosis: Progress has stalled in the published-record basin, reaching only 0.2073358864, about \(9.85\times10^{-5}\) below the record, with subsequent LP polishes producing progressively tiny gains. The image is not a genuinely jammed optimum: only about three pairs lie below the \(10^{-9}\) contact threshold, just six points have one such contact, and 67 points are nominally rattlers, while roughly 450 pairs are parked at a suspiciously uniform slack of about \(1.1\times10^{-8}\). Thus the apparent rattlers are an artefact of using a \(10^{-9}\) threshold at the same scale as the previous trust-radius/termination floor. The missing structure is a collapsed equiripple, rigid contact graph in which most points have several contacts carrying positive LP-dual weights whose tangent resultants balance, so repeated minimax polishing merely squeezes the current top pairs and contact-based surgery has been targeting the wrong points.
